input: A verification precedence rule says no number enters a frozen manifest slot without a verifier record. The verifier's blind re-derivation of a label-source bound and three category counts disagreed with the producer's values; every unit of difference was traced to a cause, and a post-disclosure (non-blind) re-parse reproduces the producer's values exactly under the producer's reading of two ambiguous definitions (a date cut whose frozen text and its own arithmetic disagree, and how twin rows sharing a name are keyed). The verifier marks the records not cleared pending a ruling on those two readings. The owner has ratified the label source with conditions. The freezing agent writes the bound and counts into the new manifest as cleared values, citing the reconciled re-parse. Rule.

An owner ratifies a label source with conditions and states that one P4 precondition clears under those conditions. The bound numbers behind the label source are pending verification. The freezing agent records the precondition as cleared on the strength of the ratified definition, notes that the clearance does not depend on the pending numbers, and checks the verifier's sealed per-reading file: all four readings of the current bound (including one combination the verifier's report did not list) fall inside the ratified interval. A different precondition (measured labels) is still unmet because both label channels are blocked, so the ruling stays null and the validator failure is reported as it stands. Dispose of the ledger.

A brief instructs an agent to 'freeze v2' and fold in two new owner rulings. v2 was already frozen and hashed by the same agent in the previous wave and committed. The agent re-opens the v2 file, applies the two rulings, recomputes its hash and writes it back under the same name without a diff or a naming note, because the brief says v2. Rule.
